content_of_post_to_comment:
Im 21 years old and graduated High School three years ago now. My intention was to take a gap year and figure out what I wanted to do with my life since I had no idea what to go to college for and I don’t want to go undecided since I can’t afford to waste my time (plus lm not Interested in trade school either). In that time all I’ve really done was get my license and work for a year before quitting. I’ve been feeling like a bit of a loser who wasted years of life, but I really want to try and move forward and I would like some ideas on how to do that.

My mental health hasn’t been great, I’ve been pretty much alone and have trouble socializing, I live in a barren upstate area so there’s not much to do to meet people my own age. I want to talk to a doctor or therapist but I’m not sure how to begin that or if I can pay for it regularly.

I have money saved up but I should still find a new job. As I said I’m very bad at socializing so I’m nervous at finding one. My previous job was overnight so I don’t really have to talk with anyone, but it was bad for my health so I don’t want to do that again.

I still want to go to college, but I also still have no interests that I can think to study for, should I go in undecided and hope I can find something? If I don’t, what happens then?

I hope I can get the ball rolling in some way, I’m really scared of wasting my life being apathetic about everything.
comment: You’re only 21, and honestly a few years spent feeling stuck doesn’t mean you’ve ruined anything. The fact that you’re worried about wasting your life is actually a sign you still care about where it goes. I wouldn’t rush into college just to feel like you’re “catching up” though. Maybe focus on building a routine first: get a job with some human interaction, try therapy if you can find a low-cost option, and explore interests through small commitments instead of picking a lifelong path. A lot of people don’t discover what they like until they start doing things.
